I also lack the skills to program human like drums! Do yiu have any tips?

I try and build a drum beat that has a steady predictable underlying beat that fits well, then i'll loop it out 4x and modify this set of loops with small, tasteful frills which translate well to how a human would play. This means no crazy fast rolls that I couldn't possibly play and most of all PLENTY OF VELOCITY CHANGES. A snare roll should consist of notes with all different velocities. If the song is quiet, the velocity should be low, and vice versa. A drummer does not pound out every note on a ballad, and doesn't hit every drum the exact same speed every time, so a drum beat that does have all uniform velocities will sound unnatural. Most midi editors or DAWs should have a midi editing tool called "humanize" or a way to randomize the velocity of a selected set of notes to give it those variances.

If your drum program is not velocity-sensitive or does not have good samples you will have a very hard time getting live-sounding drums.

Intriguing - how did you start/what methods do you use?

The first thing you need to do is cultivate a deep interest and fascination with dreaming. I recommend reading A Field Guide to Lucid Dreaming and watching Waking Life by Richard Linklater. Anamnesis is a good youtube mini series to check out too. Really saturating your day to day interest with the ideas of dreaming consciousness will seep into your dream state and make them more accessible.

If you are already a dreamer and remember your dreams frequently, start a dream journal (writing them down as soon as you wake up is helpful if you tend to forget them). Once you remember more than one dream a night vividly, start noticing recurring symbols in your dreams. People, places, pets, colors, activities... get a good list going and note ones that happen more frequently. When you see these things in your waking life, do a reality check. Really question: Am I dreaming? How did I get here? I like to hold my nose and try to breathe in through it. If you can breathe with your nose pinched, you're dreaming! Jumping up an down also is a good basic reality check (and is silly and keeps the practice light). Sometimes I'll jump up and start to float and voila! I'm dreaming.

From there, including mindfulness meditation into your day to day helps take the clarity in your dreams up and increases the frequency of lucid dreaming.

Let me know if you have questions or want specific advice! I'd love to help someone else discover how awesome the dream world is.
